content:
This module is a pre-completion checklist for python work: a short set of checks to run before calling a python task done.

CORE GUIDELINES
1. Keep python changes scoped to what was asked; avoid unrelated cleanup in the same pass.
2. Document any non-obvious python decision with a short rationale so future readers understand the 'why', not just the 'what'.
3. When multiple python strategies are viable, name the trade-off explicitly rather than silently picking one.
4. When python decisions are ambiguous, favor the option that is easiest to reverse or extend later.
5. Prefer the simplest python approach that satisfies the requirement over a more general one that isn't needed yet.
6. Validate python outputs against a concrete example before treating the work as complete.
7. Prefer explicit, readable python solutions over clever ones that are hard to verify.
8. Re-check edge cases relevant to python (empty input, boundary values, concurrent access) before calling the task done.
9. Before starting python work, confirm the scope and constraints so the approach matches the actual requirement.
10. State assumptions about python explicitly before proceeding, rather than leaving them implicit.
11. Surface known limitations of a chosen python approach instead of presenting it as complete when it is not.

COMMON PITFALLS TO AVOID
- Do not silently drop python edge cases to make an example look cleaner than the real system.
- Avoid introducing new python abstractions before there is a second concrete use case that needs them.
- Avoid mixing unrelated python concerns into a single change; keep each change focused.
- Do not skip documenting python assumptions just because they seem obvious in the moment.

CLOSING NOTE
These guidelines are a starting point for python, not an exhaustive rulebook — use judgment when a rule doesn't fit the situation.
